Let

\[
F(x)=\frac{\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{ctg}^{2} x}-\sqrt[3]{\operatorname{tg}^{2} x}}
{\sqrt[3]{\sin ^{2} x}-\sqrt[3]{\cos ^{2} x}}.
\]

For \(x\in\left(-\frac{3\pi}{2},-\pi\right)\), we have \(\sin x\neq 0\) and \(\cos x\neq 0\). Set

\[
S=\sin^2 x,\qquad C=\cos^2 x.
\]

Then \(S,C>0\) and \(S+C=1\). Also,

\[
\operatorname{ctg}^2 x=\frac{C}{S},\qquad \operatorname{tg}^2 x=\frac{S}{C}.
\]

Let \(u=S^{1/3}\) and \(v=C^{1/3}\). Then

\[
F(x)=\frac{\frac{v}{u}-\frac{u}{v}}{u-v}
=\frac{\frac{v^2-u^2}{uv}}{u-v}
=\frac{(v-u)(v+u)}{uv(u-v)}
=-\frac{u+v}{uv}.
\]

Thus

\[
F(x)=-\left(S^{-1/3}+C^{-1/3}\right).
\]

Now we need the maximum possible value of \(F(x)\), which is the negative of the minimum of

\[
g(S)=S^{-1/3}+C^{-1/3}=S^{-1/3}+(1-S)^{-1/3}.
\]

By AM-GM,

\[
S^{-1/3}+C^{-1/3}\ge 2(SC)^{-1/6}.
\]

Since \(S+C=1\),

\[
SC\le \frac14,
\]

and because \(t\mapsto t^{-1/6}\) is decreasing,

\[
(SC)^{-1/6}\ge \left(\frac14\right)^{-1/6}=2^{1/3}.
\]

Therefore

\[
S^{-1/3}+C^{-1/3}\ge 2\cdot 2^{1/3}=2^{4/3}.
\]

Equality occurs when \(S=C=\frac12\), i.e. at \(x=-\frac{5\pi}{4}\). But at that point the original denominator is \(0\), so it is not a permissible value. Hence for every permissible \(x\),

\[
F(x)<-2^{4/3}.
\]

So the smallest valid \(a\) is

\[
a=-2^{4/3}\approx -2.519842.
\]

Rounded to two decimal places,

\[
\boxed{-2.52}
\]
